A5-111.axis: sub-types (named contemporary tendencies) first; then artists by named group or circle (Neo-Geo, New Leipzig School, New Glasgow Boys, Chinese groups from the Stars to Cynical Realism, Indigenous and diaspora movements); then by country of activity, largest first, split by birth generation where a country exceeds 150; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region; artists with no recorded country grouped by the biennial or list that recorded them; within groups by birth year
A5-111.defn: The period style of painters and artists born from about 1945 who work after modernism in plural, global practices: post-colonial figurative painting, new abstraction, appropriation, art of the biennial circuit. Artists who belong to a named post-1945 movement (Neo-expressionism, Young British Artists, Pictures Generation, Superflat, Stuckism...) sit in that movement's leaf; this leaf keeps the rest.
catalogues: searchable catalogue of the Museum of Modern Art's c. 200,000 works, strong in post-1945 art
the British national collection of modern and contemporary art, every work with a page
the Guggenheim museums' collection of modern and contemporary art
American art of the 20th and 21st centuries, all works online
Hong Kong museum's collection of Asian contemporary art, including the Sigg collection of Chinese contemporary art

D5-119.axis: monumental works first; then sculptors by named group (Feminist art movement and others), then by country of activity, largest first; countries with fewer than 3 sculptors pooled by region; within groups by birth year
D5-119.defn: Sculpture by artists born from about 1945: object, figure, assemblage and installation-based work. Members of named movements (New British Sculpture, Young British Artists, Mono-ha, Land Art) sit in those leaves.
catalogues: Tate's holdings of modern and contemporary sculpture
every publicly owned artwork in the UK, including its sculpture survey of public and outdoor sculpture
MoMA's painting and sculpture holdings, searchable by artist
the Musée national d'art moderne collection, over 100,000 works

M1-1.axis: sub-types first; then artists by named movement or group (Light and Space, Mono-ha, Gutai Art Association, light art, feminist art), then by country of activity, largest first; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region; artists with no recorded country grouped by the biennial that recorded them; within groups by birth year
catalogues: MoMA's holdings of installation and environment works, searchable by artist
Tate's term page linking every Tate installation work
Dia's collection of large-scale works and long-term installations
Pittsburgh museum of room-sized installation art and its archive of past installations

M1-2.axis: artists by named group or school first (Art & Language, Moscow Conceptualists, Photoconceptualism, CAYC, General Idea, New Art Practice in Yugoslavia, NSK, Neo-conceptual art); then by country of activity, largest first; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region; within groups by birth year
catalogues: MoMA's term page with its conceptual works
Tate's term page linking its conceptual works
digitised archives of Moscow Conceptualism and Russian unofficial art

M2-5.axis: sub-types first; then artists by named group, then by country of activity, largest first; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region; artists with no recorded country grouped by the biennial that recorded them; within groups by birth year
catalogues: archive of over 2,000 works of net art and born-digital art since 1999
scholarly database of digital and media art works and artists
Karlsruhe Centre for Art and Media: media art collection and archive
Amsterdam collection and distribution of media art

L2-51.axis: sub-types (techniques) first; then artists by named group, then by country of activity, largest first; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region; within groups by birth year
catalogues: crowd-sourced world map of street-art works, over 100,000 pieces
photographed street art from partner institutions and cities
Tate's term page on street art and graffiti

YBA.label: Young British Artists
YBA.defn: Loose group of artists, many from Goldsmiths College, who showed together from the Freeze exhibition (London, 1988) and were collected by Charles Saatchi, culminating in Sensation (Royal Academy, 1997): Hirst, Emin, Lucas, Whiteread, the Chapman brothers, Ofili, Gordon.
catalogues: Tate's term page linking the YBAs' works in the national collection
the gallery of the collector who championed the group, with its exhibition archive
UK national loan collection, rich in 1990s British art
YBA.axis: by phase: Goldsmiths circle and Freeze (1988); the Saatchi and Sensation (1997) generation; the Turner Prize and film/video wing; within groups by birth year

NBS.label: New British Sculpture
NBS.defn: British sculptors who emerged around 1980–85, mostly shown by the Lisson Gallery, making sculpture from found, industrial and natural materials with a renewed interest in object and image: Cragg, Woodrow, Deacon, Gormley, Kapoor, Wilding.
catalogues: Tate's term page linking the group's works in the collection
the London gallery that showed the group, with artist pages and exhibition histories
every publicly owned sculpture in the UK, searchable by artist
NBS.axis: by group: the Lisson Gallery generation of the early 1980s; within the group by birth year

PIC.label: Pictures Generation
PIC.defn: American artists of the late 1970s–80s, named after Douglas Crimp's Pictures exhibition (Artists Space, New York, 1977), who used appropriation, montage and photography to examine mass-media images: Sherrie Levine, Richard Prince, Barbara Kruger, Robert Longo, Cindy Sherman.
catalogues: the Metropolitan Museum's survey exhibition of the group
MoMA's holdings of the group's photographs and paintings
American art collection with the group's works online
PIC.axis: by circle: the Artists Space Pictures show (1977) and CalArts circle; the wider New York appropriation circle; within groups by birth year

REL.label: Relational art
REL.defn: Art of the 1990s whose material is human relations and their social context, theorised by Nicolas Bourriaud in Relational Aesthetics (1998): Tiravanija's cooked meals, Gillick's discussion platforms, Höller's slides.
catalogues: Tate's term page linking relational works in the collection
includes the theanyspacewhatever (2008) group of relational artists
REL.axis: by group: the artists Bourriaud names in Relational Aesthetics (1998); within the group by birth year

FBC.label: Franco-Belgian comics
FBC.defn: French-language comics (bande dessinée) of Belgium, France and Switzerland, published as albums: from the Brussels and Marcinelle schools to adult auteur comics and the graphic memoir (Hergé, Franquin, Moebius, Bilal, Satrapi).
catalogues: database of over 400,000 French-language comic albums and their authors
Cité internationale de la bande dessinée et de l'image
Angoulême museum and library holding the French legal-deposit comics collection
FBC.axis: by school and phase: the Belgian publishers' tradition (ligne claire, atom style, Spirou); humour series and gag strips; adult and auteur bande dessinée; L'Association and the graphic memoir; within groups by birth year
